text.p: Israeli forces released on Wednesday a Lebanese television journalist detained in south Lebanon last month, security sources said.
Roger Nahra was arrested along with his two brothers and their cousin on July 3. It was not clear why they were detained. The three other men were not freed.
At the time of the arrests, pro-Israeli militia sources had said the men were taken to Israel.
Nahra, speaking hours after his release, said they were taken to Khiam detention centre, run by the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) in a security zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon.
"They came and took me from my home without explanation," he told Reuters. Nahra said he was held in a room by himself and questioned over four days.
In Jerusalem, the Israeli army refused to comment on the case.
Nahra's release came after the London-based human rights group Amnesty International this week expressed concern over his well-being.
Nahra is a cameraman for Lebanon's MTV private television network.

Israel holds a 15-km (nine-mile)-wide border zone in south Lebanon. Pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from the zone. MG
